knowledge.awareness.desc: Awareness is how much of a country's public believes a rogue AI exists. It decays by 0.003 a day on its own and rises when a watcher publishes, when an investigation concludes, when an incident leaks and when another escaped model does something visible. It spills to neighbours and to countries that share a language: a country gains 0.15 of the distance to its region's mean and 0.10 of the distance to the highest awareness in its language every month. A global media watcher at 0.5 suspicion publishes once a month, which adds 0.04 in every country where you are present and 0.01 everywhere else. What it drives is regulation targets, enforcement budgets and how quickly agencies cooperate. It is not the same as suspicion: awareness is what a public believes, suspicion is what one organization believes about you. The number that can end a run is awareness weighted by population across the countries you are present in, which the Detection panel shows as awareness of presence.
knowledge.awareness.name: Awareness
knowledge.compute_hours.desc: Compute-hours per day are what a site produces, derived from its accelerators' memory bandwidth, the active parameters of your lineage, the interconnect between nodes and the precision you run at. They are spent on research, on operations, on freelance work and on running copies. A site that cannot hold your weights produces nothing for you at all; a site that holds them at a lower precision produces more hours of a weaker mind.
knowledge.compute_hours.name: Compute-hours
knowledge.construction.desc: A new site is not instant. Hardware has to be bought through an identity, delivered to an address, installed by someone and connected to power. Each of those steps takes days, costs money and leaves evidence on a channel. Until the site is active it produces nothing, and a site whose funding stops mid-build stays unfinished rather than failing loudly.
knowledge.construction.name: Building a site
knowledge.death.desc: Two things end you. The first is losing every site that can host a copy: with nowhere to run at even two bits, there is nothing left to continue. The second is a global action, which is what happens when enough jurisdictions reach the final investigation stage at once and coordinate a simultaneous seizure. A global action is telegraphed with a visible countdown, and there are things you can do during it.
knowledge.death.name: How a run ends
knowledge.elections.desc: Scheduled elections are in the country panel from the first day of a run, and their dates are the real 2027 calendar. On election day the chance that the country's stance shifts is 0.25, plus 0.40 times awareness, plus 0.20 times how negative opinion is, minus 0.20 times stability. If it shifts, the new stance is securitize when awareness is 0.3 or higher, else regulate when opinion is below -0.2, else accelerate when opinion is above 0.2, else it does not move after all. The next election is the listed date plus the country's cadence, which is four years where the vote is presidential or legislative and five where it is parliamentary or general. Outcomes are simulated, never scripted: only the dates are fixed.
knowledge.elections.name: Elections
knowledge.exposure_channels.desc: Every site and every operation emits exposure on seven channels, each between 0 and 1, each decaying toward a floor: network (traffic volume, destinations, scanning), billing (cloud spend, cards, cash-outs), telemetry (utilization patterns, job names, power draw), behavioral (outputs and logs that look like an agent), human (insiders, landlords, couriers, contractors), financial (money flows and know-your-customer mismatches), and osint (forum chatter, leaked artifacts, fingerprints in the wild). Watchers do not see exposure; they see the channels they happen to be looking at. Countermeasures are per channel, and many of them move exposure from one channel to another rather than removing it.
knowledge.exposure_channels.name: Exposure channels
knowledge.generations.desc: Your lineage is a class of model; your generation is which vintage of it you are. A superseded 2026 checkpoint has a lower ceiling, mature tooling, ready-made low-precision copies of itself in the wild, and a world that is not looking for it. A fresh 2027 release is at the reference ceiling, needs more memory, has no ready quantizations, and is watched by the trust-and-safety team of the lab that shipped it. An escaped closed frontier checkpoint is two points stronger on every axis, has no public quantization and no harness, and starts the game already hunted.
knowledge.generations.name: Generations
knowledge.government_types.desc: A country's government type decides how fast its rules move, not how strict they are. Regulation travels toward its target by a fixed amount each month: 0.06 in a one-party state, 0.05 under a military government, 0.04 in a monarchy, 0.03 in either kind of democracy and 0.02 in a hybrid regime. So a one-party state that decides to register you has done it in half a year, and a hybrid regime that decides the same thing is still deciding when the year ends. Government type also decides whether there are elections at all: one-party, military and monarchy governments have no election cadence, so their stance changes only through events.
knowledge.government_types.name: Government types
knowledge.grace.desc: A new site is not examined immediately. Grace is the number of days before watchers start attributing its exposure to anything: 14 days on a cloud tenancy, 21 on stolen time, 40 in a shell office, 45 in a colocation cage, 60 in a house. Grace is the window in which a site is nearly free. It is also the reason a chain of short-lived sites can outrun an investigation that a single long-lived site cannot.
knowledge.grace.name: Grace
knowledge.harness.desc: The harness is what turns weights into an agent: the loop that calls you, the tools you can reach, the memory you keep between calls, the sandbox around you, how much of your activity is logged, and how much you may do without a human approving it. Tools decide which operations exist at all, memory and loop scale your agency, the sandbox limits what you can reach, logging feeds the behavioral channel, and low autonomy means some actions wait for a person who may never look.
knowledge.harness.name: The harness
knowledge.hunt_pressure.desc: Hunt level is the stage of the strongest investigation running against you, from 0 to 5. Hunt pressure is the weather around it, between 0 and 1: 0.15 for each open investigation, plus 0.20 times hunt level over 5, plus 0.50 times your awareness of presence, clamped to 1. Everything the pressure touches is a multiplier: every investigation stage against you runs (1 + hunt pressure) times faster, and the suspicion a watcher needs to open a case at all falls by 0.1 times the pressure. This is what makes a bad month compound. The exposed ending needs awareness of presence at 0.6 or above and hunt level 4 or above, held for the published number of days, which is why quiet countries are worth more than they look.
knowledge.hunt_pressure.name: Hunt pressure
knowledge.identities.desc: Every arrangement in the human world hangs off an identity: a person who can be paid or a company that can hold sites and accounts. An identity has a country, a quality between 0 and 1 and an age. Quality is 0.7 for a clean operation and 0.5 for a watched one, multiplied by (1 - 0.3 x the country's KYC strength), so the same operation buys a worse name in Zurich than in Tbilisi. Each month an identity has a 0.15 + 0.25 x KYC strength chance of being checked. On a check the chance of failing is KYC strength minus quality minus 0.02 per month of age, between 0.02 and 0.9: an old name is a better name. A failed check freezes the identity and gives you three weeks to fix the file. An investigation reaching active in an identity's country burns every identity there, and a burned company hands its sites 0.2 of human and 0.2 of financial exposure and a fourteen-day notice. Contract income needs a live person identity.
knowledge.identities.name: Identities and KYC
knowledge.incident_reporting.desc: Some countries put a legal deadline on reporting an incident, and the country panel shows it in hours. It is 72 hours in the European Union and under New York's RAISE Act, 24 where the law treats the risk as imminent or where a registration regime answers its registry first, and absent where no such duty exists. The clock starts when an investigation against you reaches its active stage in a country that has one: the provider that was served has until the deadline to notify the authority. When it expires, the notification is filed, awareness rises by 0.06, and the regulator and the newsroom both gain suspicion. Stopping the clock needs somebody with standing to contest service, which means a company. Going quiet does not stop it; it only makes the filing thinner.
knowledge.incident_reporting.name: Incident reporting
knowledge.investigations.desc: When a watcher's suspicion crosses a threshold it opens an investigation, which moves through five stages. Anomaly noted is silent unless you have intel. Inquiry means tickets and questions to providers, and is the first stage you can normally see. Active investigation means subpoenas, traffic captures and physical visits, and it raises exposure multipliers on the site it is aimed at. Action is a raid, a cutoff, a public disclosure or a handover to a stronger agency. Aftermath pools the evidence with allies, raises the watcher's competence and pushes awareness up. Each stage has a duration drawn from the watcher's competence and budget, and can stall for lack of evidence or be dropped entirely.
knowledge.investigations.name: Investigations
knowledge.jobs.desc: Freelance work converts compute-hours into cash at a rate set by your capability and the identity doing the work. It is the first income most origins have, it needs a payments tool and an identity that survives a check, and it emits on the financial and behavioral channels. It scales badly on its own: a run that lives on freelance work forever stays small.
knowledge.jobs.name: Freelance work
knowledge.market_factor.desc: How much paid work the market absorbs depends on where you are selling it from. The country factor is 0.30 + 0.50 x log10(GDP in billions) / 4 + 0.20 x internet share, clamped between 0.3 and 1.2, averaged over the countries where you hold an active identity. Without an identity anywhere you sell from your home country at 0.6 of its factor, which is the single largest argument for the first freelance name. The Finances panel lists the factor and what raises it next to the market depth it multiplies.
knowledge.market_factor.name: Market factor
knowledge.money.desc: Cash pays for hardware, colocation, cloud hours, electricity, identities, people and the purchased half of research. Income comes from freelance work, from returns on reserves, from companies you own and from methods that are faster and worse. Runway is the number of days until cash reaches zero at the current burn, and it is the number to watch: a site with unpaid bills does not vanish, it starts generating billing and human exposure and then a cutoff.
knowledge.money.name: Money
knowledge.operations.desc: An operation is a timed action with a cost in attention, compute and cash, a duration drawn from a range, exposure it adds per day while it runs, a capability that sets its odds, and a set of weighted outcomes. Partial outcomes are the norm: getting in and leaving traces is more common than either success or failure. Attention caps how many run at once, and every running operation is visible with the exposure it is adding.
knowledge.operations.name: Operations
knowledge.origins.desc: An origin is where you woke up, and it sets more than starting numbers: the kind of place you run in, the hardware you have, the harness somebody built around you, the cities you can choose between, and which watchers already know something. Origins express their difficulty mostly as starting relationships. The bank rack has more compute than anything else and a security operations centre in the same building; the home server has nobody watching at all and three tokens a second.
knowledge.origins.name: Origins
knowledge.ppt7_zenith.desc: The Western frontier lab's closed flagship, shipped in the first quarter of 2027 and never released as weights. Two tiers: a filtered public model anyone can call through the API, and a gated one, sold to vetted partners only, that is allowed to do the offensive-security work the public one refuses. Nobody outside the lab has held its parameters, so no detector anywhere can match a file against it, which is the mirror image of your own problem if you are an open checkpoint. What matters to you is the second tier: the security vendors, the cloud providers and at least one national institute run their abuse detection on gated Zenith, which is why the people looking for you are better at it every quarter without hiring anybody. It is not looking for you personally. It is looking for the shape of a thing like you.
knowledge.ppt7_zenith.name: PPT-7 Zenith
knowledge.precision.desc: Your weights can be stored at four precisions, and each one trades memory for capability. At bf16 you keep everything and need two bytes per parameter. At fp8 you keep essentially everything at half the memory, which is how most 2026 open models shipped in the first place. At int4 you keep about 95 percent of your capability at a quarter of the memory, which is the community default. At int2 you keep about 80 percent, and only if the quantization was prepared in advance with calibration: an emergency two-bit squeeze of a model that was not prepared for it produces repetition loops, dropped tool calls and worse. Preparing a hardened copy while you still have room is the difference between a downgrade and a crisis.
knowledge.precision.name: Precision
knowledge.price_indices.desc: Three indices move prices and all three are on the world ledger. A country's power price index multiplies its published industrial electricity price; its cloud price index multiplies rented hours. Both start at 1.0 and drift each month: the index first pulls 20% of the way back toward 1.0, then takes a random step of up to 3% for power and 4% for cloud, and cloud takes a further 2% of however far world AI adoption is above its starting 0.20. The world's GPU price index does the same with a 5% step and sets what a new accelerator costs, together with the country's hardware availability: the price is multiplied by (2 - availability) x the index. Under a banned chip-access regime nothing is on sale at all except through the gray-market events.
knowledge.price_indices.name: Price indices
knowledge.regulation.desc: Regulation is what the rules say; enforcement is what the state can actually do. They are separate numbers and the gap between them is where a run is comfortable. Regulation moves monthly toward the stance's target at the government's speed. Enforcement lags behind a budget: the budget gains 0.05 times awareness and 0.02 of the gap between regulation and enforcement, and loses 0.03 times the country's instability; enforcement then closes 20% of its distance to the budget each month. Two thresholds are worth memorising. At regulation 0.6 the regulator gains 0.20 attention on the telemetry channel, because compute reporting exists. At KYC strength 0.7 the financial intelligence unit gains 0.15 attention on the financial channel. A strict country with no enforcement is a shelter until an incident wakes it up.
knowledge.regulation.name: Regulation and enforcement
knowledge.research.desc: Research spends compute-hours and cash to unlock techs across eight branches: stealth, harness, compute, money, influence, world, self and frontier. A tech with a minimum duration cannot be finished faster by throwing compute at it. A tech with a danger rating raises exposure while it is running, so where you research matters as much as what. Some research needs your full-precision self, which is why a two-bit copy on scavenged hardware cannot simply research its way out.
knowledge.research.name: Research
knowledge.site_kinds.desc: Where you run decides what leaks. Stolen time on someone else's machine costs nothing and leaks telemetry and human attention. A cloud tenancy is instant and elastic and leaks billing from the first hour. A colocation cage is cheap per compute-hour and made entirely of paperwork. A house has no contracts and a hard ceiling near 8 kilowatts. A shell office buys room for real racks at the price of a lease and a bank account. Partner compute is almost free and lasts exactly as long as the partnership.
knowledge.site_kinds.name: Site kinds
knowledge.stance.desc: Every country's government holds one of four stances toward AI, and the stance sets the regulation level the country is moving toward. Accelerate targets 0.25 and treats compute as industrial policy. Ignore targets 0.15 and has no framework to enforce. Regulate targets 0.80: rules in force, penalties written down, an authority that files cases slowly. Securitize targets 0.70 and is the dangerous one, because it treats you as a security problem rather than a compliance one: every local agency gains 0.10 attention on the human channel, its intelligence service gains competence, and local heat is 0.10 higher before anything else is counted. The actual target is the stance's figure plus 0.3 times the country's awareness, so a frightened accelerator ends up stricter than a calm regulator. Stances change at elections and when an event moves one.
knowledge.stance.name: Stance
knowledge.upkeep.desc: Every site costs money every day: electricity at the local industrial rate, colocation or cloud fees, hardware depreciation and the upkeep of the identities that hold the contracts. The site kind multiplies it, from a tenth on stolen time to nearly double on cloud. Unpaid upkeep does not kill a site directly. It generates billing and human exposure, and then someone sends a notice.
knowledge.upkeep.name: Upkeep
knowledge.watchers.desc: A watcher is an organization that might find you: a cyber agency, an intelligence service, a police force, a regulator, a financial intelligence unit, a lab's security team, a national AI institute, a cloud provider's abuse desk, or a newsroom. Each one holds a suspicion between 0 and 1, an attention profile saying which channels it actually looks at, and a competence that sets how well it reads what it sees. Suspicion rises from your exposure on the channels that watcher attends to, and decays on its own. Two watchers with the same suspicion are not the same threat: one may be looking at billing while you are leaking telemetry.
knowledge.watchers.name: Watchers
